findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all eight cohorts, and in the same MSCCR patients it is higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. It is only mildly raised in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399], so it mostly marks local inflammation. Caveat: CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk rise most likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a tissue-intrinsic change.

The CXCR2 change holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex in MSCCR (adjusted and unadjusted log2FC are nearly identical), so it is not a sampling-site, age or sex artefact. This does not exclude a cell-composition effect.

CXCL8 (IL-8), the main CXCR1/CXCR2 ligand, shows a pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864] with all eight cohorts up. Together with CXCR1, CXCR2 and CXCL1/CXCL5 this forms a coherent neutrophil-recruitment axis; the signal is partly neutrophil- and myeloid-derived, and the chemokine axis is more likely a marker of local inflammation than a primary driver.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]). The paired inflamed vs non-inflamed difference is [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6828], with a small residual rise in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.535]. It is an interferon-driven local inflammation marker; it comes from immune and epithelial cells, which this specialist cannot separate.

MMP3 has one of the largest pooled increases (log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901]), up in all eight cohorts, and it replicates at protein level in an independent proteomics study of inflamed mucosa (log2 ratio [gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]). The protein change is much smaller than the RNA change. MMP3 is stromal and inflammatory in origin.

CHI3L1 is strongly and consistently up (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875], eight of eight cohorts up). It holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=3.732]). The proteomics change is small and the authors did not call it significant, so protein-level support is weaker than the RNA signal.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis gene, is among the most robust losses (pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838], down in all eight cohorts). It is not changed in non-inflamed mucosa of the same cohort [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so the loss is local to inflamed mucosa. It is also lost at protein level [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094], and holds after adjustment. A biomarker of epithelial metabolic collapse, not a plausible drug target.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss among top genes (log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]), down significantly in most cohorts. Together with CLDN8, PCK1, SLC26A2 and GUCA2A/B this is a mature-absorptive-colonocyte program lost in inflamed mucosa; these are biomarkers of epithelial dedifferentiation rather than targets.

DUOX2 (with DUOXA2, the largest pooled increase) is strongly up in all eight cohorts (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412]), an epithelial reactive-oxygen/barrier-stress response with no drug and no genetic support in the ranking; between-cohort heterogeneity is high, so the size is not stable even though the direction is.

S100A8 (and S100A9/S100A12) is strongly up (pooled log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77]) in all eight cohorts. Caveat: these are neutrophil/myeloid genes (calprotectin), so the bulk rise mainly reflects infiltrating cells; useful as an activity biomarker, not evidence of a change in epithelial cells.

REG1A has a large pooled increase (log2FC [gene=REG1A; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.486]) but is the least reproducible of the top genes: six of eight cohorts significant up, not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort or the adult colon cohort, and heterogeneity is very high. The size is driven by paediatric rectum cohorts.

JAK2 is the genetics-supported, drug-tractable target with a modest expression change (pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874]; eight of eight cohorts up). Its rank comes from genetic association and tractability, not from the size of the expression change.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974]) with genetic association in Open Targets, consistent with an interferon-induced feedback checkpoint in inflamed mucosa. It is an immune/epithelial-shared gene, so the bulk rise may partly reflect infiltrating myeloid cells.

caveats: Bulk biopsy data: increases in neutrophil and myeloid genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8/9/12, TREM1, IL1B) may come from infiltrating cells rather than from a change inside the tissue; the cell-context specialist must confirm this.
Microarray cohorts compress fold changes, so sizes were not compared across platforms; heterogeneity between cohorts is high so pooled sizes are approximate.
Proteomics covers only a subset of genes and a small independent cohort; absent protein data is not evidence against a gene.
Adjusted analysis covers only MSCCR; the paired and non-inflamed contrasts come from a single registry.
Convergence ranking mixes expression with literature and drug history, so top-ranked chemokine genes are partly favoured by tractability.
